purpose: Select the next revival candidate by EVIDENCE from the committed ranking, not intuition, and record the three traps found while doing so.

trap_1_duplicate_files.finding: Ranks 4,5,6,7 have BYTE-IDENTICAL n=64, lift=14.01, wr=65.62 on XAUUSD-M5. They are the SAME LPSB layer recorded under four different filenames: S351 (twice, two naming conventions), S355, S376.
trap_1_duplicate_files.why_it_matters: Ranking blindly by rank_score would have had me 'revive' a layer S431 already shipped, and the duplicate rows also INFLATE the apparent size of the POOL-READY tier: of 38 rows, a substantial share are aliases rather than distinct opportunities.
trap_1_duplicate_files.action: De-duplicated by (strategy_id, card, n) fingerprint before choosing.

trap_2_live_layers_in_the_candidate_list.finding: The ranking does not know which layers are already SHIPPED. Of the top 10 rows, 7 belong to layers already live in local-mobile/app.bundle.mjs: S355, S312, S354, S344, S334, S374, S323.
trap_2_live_layers_in_the_candidate_list.method: Extracted every S-number from the built bundle and cross-referenced. Verified against the '// star Sxxx' layer registration comments rather than bare number matches.

trap_3_my_own_false_alarm_recorded.claim_i_made: I initially grepped for 'SOS' in the bundle, got 15 hits, and concluded SoS logic was live under a different ID.
trap_3_my_own_false_alarm_recorded.reality: All 15 hits were substrings of toISOString(). The grep was naive and the conclusion was WRONG.
trap_3_my_own_false_alarm_recorded.correction: Re-checked with the layer-registration comment pattern and with an explicit S1xx scan: ZERO S1xx layers are live. S171 SoS is genuinely absent from the shipped portfolio.
trap_3_my_own_false_alarm_recorded.why_recorded: This mission's own history (E-13, BUG-NULLUNCOND) shows that the dangerous failures here are the ones that run silently and produce a confident wrong answer. A grep that matches a date function and returns 15 confident hits is precisely that shape, so it is logged rather than quietly fixed.

chain_already_closed.note: S202 named an unfinished next step, and I checked whether it was done rather than assuming it was not. It WAS done, three times over.
chain_already_closed.S202: SoS(LONG) on XAUUSD-H1 passed a hard gate at +$12,765, WR 48.3%, PF 1.69, SL250/TP750/mh96, with 62 parameter combinations passing => robust, not a single overfit setting. Market Inertia(SHORT) on H1 was dead.
chain_already_closed.S203: Overlap vs SoS-M15: daily PnL corr +0.268 (low), but the genuinely independent remainder was only +$322 on n=87 with walk-forward [-1574,-453,+1087,+1746] => unstable. Independent-layer and replacement routes both REJECTED.
chain_already_closed.S204: Filtering that independent remainder with ATR14>ATR100 stabilised it: +$1,445, WR 54.8%, n=31, WF 4/4 positive, with 5 gate-passing combinations all containing ATR => robust.
chain_already_closed.S205: DECISIVE at the time: measured the remainder against the UNION of all gold LONG layers' trading days (1,534 days). Genuinely new share was 5 trades, net -$27 => non-incremental, REJECT.
chain_already_closed.S206: H1 context as an MTF confirmation filter ON the live SoS-M15: every filter REDUCED net, best delta -$2,696 => no improvement.

the_reframing.observation: S205's rejection rests entirely on the claim that ~98% of SoS-H1's trading days were already covered by the then-existing gold LONG portfolio, which explicitly included SoS-M15, Overnight, Monday and TurnOfMonth layers.
the_reframing.but: That portfolio NO LONGER EXISTS. Under RQS2 v2.6 the live set is S312, S344, S355, S356, S431, S432 - and ZERO S1xx layers survive. SoS-M15 itself is gone, and the Overnight layer is the very S139/S434 family I proved eternally dead this mission.
the_reframing.implication: The double-counting objection that killed S202-S205 was measured against a coverage union that has since been dismantled. It must be RE-MEASURED against the current live portfolio before the layer can be called dead. This is not a loophole: it is the project's own overlap rule, which requires overlap to be measured against the ACTUAL portfolio, applied to a portfolio that changed.
the_reframing.status: HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. The new coverage union has not been computed yet. It is entirely possible the current six live layers still cover SoS-H1's days, in which case the REJECT stands and I will report that.

decision: Adopt S435 = revival of S202/S204 'SoS-H1 + ATR14>ATR100' as a candidate INDEPENDENT layer, re-adjudicated under RQS2 v2.6 against the CURRENT live portfolio's coverage union.
why_this_candidate_over_the_alternatives: It is non-time-based price action (Al Brooks chapter 19 structure), whereas both my ACCEPTs this mission were time/structure based - directly addressing common mistake 1.

Its prior failure mode was NOT statistical weakness: S204 showed WF 4/4 positive and 5 robust gate-passing filter combinations. It was rejected for REDUNDANCY, a property of the portfolio rather than of the layer - and the portfolio changed.
Redundancy is the one rejection reason in the archive that can be overturned WITHOUT weakening any gate, so pursuing it cannot become common mistake 8.
It already carries a measured per-timeframe geometry lesson (H1 wants TP750 vs M15's TP450), consistent with common mistake 6.
pre_registered_risks: n is small: S204's filtered independent remainder was n=31. Under RQS2 v2.6 that will likely fail H4/H3 on power alone, exactly as S434 did. The unfiltered SoS-H1+ATR set is n=267 (S202) / larger in S205, which is the set I should adjudicate.
n_trials must be carried honestly: the S202 battery swept 267 variants. That is a heavy multiplicity burden and will raise the H5 bar substantially. I will count it rather than reset it to 1.
